fixture.safe_retry_predicate: Treat an existing digest as idempotent replay only if current_claim_fence == candidate.fence AND finalization_slot == digest(candidate.full_record). Digest equality alone is insufficient after a fence advance.

minimum_safe_transition_reclamation_rule.finalized_key_rule: A fence advance never clears or overwrites a completed finalization slot. For the same operation/payload/idempotency key, a nonempty finalized slot remains immutable provenance and bars reclamation/re-execution even after the active claim fence advances.
minimum_safe_transition_reclamation_rule.claim_reclamation_boundary: Only an unfinalized claim may be reclaimed under a newer fence, and that must use a distinct successor claim generation that atomically proves the newer current fence and records the predecessor claim/fence as immutable history. This fixture does not prove that orphan-claim rule; it only proves that completed finalization history must not be erased to regain liveness.
minimum_safe_transition_reclamation_rule.provenance_preservation: Retain digest(R10), F10, effect digest E10, and predecessor generation g8 as immutable historical evidence; never convert the completed slot back to ABSENT.

observations: After advancing current_claim_fence from F10 to F11, historical digest(R10) equality remains true but the joint retry predicate fails because R10 carries F10.
The modeled stale retry therefore produces no repository transition and no duplicate finalization effect.
For a completed finalization key, liveness recovery cannot safely be implemented by clearing the historical slot; provenance and completion identity must remain immutable.
inference: Within this modeled repository-finalization scope, fencing must participate in replay authorization even when the full historical record digest matches exactly. A newer fence invalidates replay authority of a completed older-fence record, while the completed record itself remains immutable history. Safe reclamation, if needed, belongs only to a separate unfinalized-claim path and requires a successor-generation protocol; that orphan-claim case remains untested.
